git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(sensors): stop the skipped-gate sensor overstating its own activity

Found by checking the live sensor ledger rather than trusting the tests: the
hook recorded `ran: true` on every Stop, including for lanes that own no
planning gates, where detectSkippedGates early-returns. This repo's lane is
"loop" and it had already logged rows saying the sensor worked.

That is the same dishonesty this wave has been about, aimed at the value meter:
a control that reports maximum activity while being constantly inapplicable
cannot be judged on whether it earns its keep — which is exactly the judgement
sensor-outcomes.jsonl exists to support.

Root cause is a conflation I have been calling out elsewhere and then committed
myself: detectSkippedGates returns [] both for "not applicable" and for
"applicable, nothing wrong", and the caller could not tell them apart. New
appliesTo(lane) makes it explicit; the hook records nothing when the sensor has
nothing to say, and carries `target` (the phases flagged, or "none") when it
does — so a row now means the sensor really looked.

Verified live, not by inspection: on lane "loop" the row count is unchanged
across a Stop; in a synthetic build-lane project the hook both surfaces the
advisory and writes target:"brd".

Also checked while here, no change needed: the modified Stop hook runs in 37ms
of its 5000ms budget, has logged no new hook-errors since it landed, and
degrades silently when state or receipts are absent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
